findings.evidence: lock a Member account after 5 consecutive failed login attempts within a 10-minute window
findings.rationale: Specifies when to lock the account, but omits the lockout duration and the unlock or recovery condition (as well as the response returned when a locked account attempts to log in).

findings.evidence: notify him
findings.rationale: The pronoun 'him' has an ambiguous antecedent; it is unclear whether the Librarian, the Member, or the Guarantor should be notified.

findings.evidence: TBD minutes
findings.rationale: Contains an unresolved 'TBD' placeholder instead of a concrete token expiration duration.

findings.evidence: user-friendly, easy to navigate, loads rapidly, standard connections
findings.rationale: Uses subjective and unmeasurable terms ('user-friendly', 'easy to navigate', 'loads rapidly', 'standard connections') without objective usability or performance criteria.

findings.evidence: TBD consecutive times
findings.rationale: Contains an unresolved 'TBD' placeholder instead of specifying the maximum number of consecutive renewals.

findings.evidence: validate item eligibility within 2 seconds and issue the loan receipt
findings.rationale: Only specifies the happy-path outcome (issuing the loan receipt) and omits what the system must do if item eligibility validation fails or the barcode cannot be validated.

findings.evidence: the allowed maximum number of active hold requests
findings.rationale: References 'the allowed maximum number' without specifying a concrete numeric limit anywhere in the specification.

findings.evidence: borrow up to 8 physical items simultaneously
findings.rationale: Allows a Member in good standing to borrow up to 8 physical items simultaneously, conflicting with SD-009 which caps simultaneous checkouts at 5 physical items.

findings.evidence: 21 calendar days from the checkout timestamp
findings.rationale: Sets the standard loan period for circulating print books to 21 calendar days, conflicting with SD-010 which sets it to 14 calendar days.

findings.evidence: self-register online with only an email address and immediately check out physical books without Librarian ID verification
findings.rationale: Permits unverified visitors to self-register with only an email address and immediately check out books without ID verification, directly contradicting SD-001 which requires a Librarian to verify government-issued photo ID and record full name, email, and phone number before creating an account.

findings.evidence: remain held indefinitely until the requesting Member explicitly cancels the hold
findings.rationale: Requires reserved items on the pickup shelf to be held indefinitely until cancelled by the Member, contradicting SD-011 which limits the hold to exactly 72 hours before automatic cancellation.

findings.evidence: send an overdue email and/or suspend borrowing privileges and/or apply a penalty flag
findings.rationale: Uses chained 'and/or' coordination, leaving it ambiguous which combination of the three actions must be executed and under what conditions.

findings.evidence: shall be reviewed, approved, and recorded
findings.rationale: Uses passive voice without identifying which actor, role, or system component is responsible for reviewing, approving, and recording fine waiver requests.

findings.evidence: if appropriate
findings.rationale: Uses the subjective weak qualifier 'if appropriate' without defining objective criteria for when SMS due-date alerts should be dispatched.

findings.evidence: TBD years
findings.rationale: Contains an unresolved 'TBD' placeholder instead of a defined retention period for payment receipts.

findings.evidence: $1.25 USD per overdue day per item with no maximum cap
findings.rationale: Specifies an overdue fine of $1.25 USD per day with no cap, conflicting with SD-019 which specifies $0.50 USD per day capped at $20.00 USD per item.

findings.evidence: renew borrowed items online at any time regardless of any unpaid overdue fine balance
findings.rationale: Allows Members to renew items regardless of unpaid overdue fines, directly contradicting SD-020 which blocks renewals when unpaid fines exceed $5.00 USD.

findings.evidence: Patron's active loan count ... Patron profile screen
findings.rationale: Introduces the undefined synonym 'Patron' instead of the standard term 'Member' used throughout the rest of the specification (e.g., SD-001 and SD-009).

findings.evidence: quickly, many users
findings.rationale: Uses unquantified vague terms ('quickly', 'many users') without specifying concrete latency targets or concurrent user counts.

findings.evidence: where possible
findings.rationale: Uses the weak optional qualifier 'where possible', making the requirement untestable by failing to define when highlighting is required versus omitted.

findings.evidence: sufficient ISBN matching accuracy, acceptable response times
findings.rationale: Uses vague qualitative adjectives ('sufficient', 'acceptable') without defining measurable accuracy or response-time thresholds.

findings.evidence: efficiently, large batch MARC21 files, noticeable system slowdown
findings.rationale: Uses vague terms ('efficiently', 'large', 'noticeable system slowdown') without specifying file size, throughput, or performance degradation bounds.

findings.evidence: shall detect the active references
findings.rationale: States only that the Catalog Service shall detect active loans or holds upon deletion attempts, without specifying the resulting action (such as blocking deletion, logging, or returning an error).

findings.evidence: TBD intervals
findings.rationale: Contains an unresolved 'TBD' placeholder instead of a concrete database backup schedule interval.

findings.evidence: important administrative actions, in a timely manner, appropriate period
findings.rationale: Uses vague, undefined terms ('important', 'in a timely manner', 'appropriate period') without enumerating audited actions or specifying concrete logging latency and retention durations.

findings.evidence: shall log event FAILOVER-01
findings.rationale: Only requires logging event FAILOVER-01 when the primary database node becomes unreachable, omitting the actual failover or recovery actions (such as promoting a standby node or alerting an Administrator).

findings.evidence: adequate transport security, clear error messages
findings.rationale: Uses vague terms ('adequate transport security', 'clear error messages') without specifying concrete protocols (e.g., TLS version) or error-message requirements.

findings.evidence: any Member password of at least 8 characters
findings.rationale: Accepts any Member password of at least 8 characters with no character-class restrictions, conflicting with SD-002 which requires at least 12 characters containing uppercase, lowercase, and numeric characters.

findings.evidence: 60 minutes of user inactivity
findings.rationale: Keeps web portal sessions active for 60 minutes of inactivity, conflicting with SD-004 which terminates sessions after 15 minutes of inactivity.

findings.evidence: encrypt all Member passwords using reversible AES-256 encryption so Administrators can decrypt and retrieve forgotten passwords
findings.rationale: Requires reversible AES-256 encryption so Administrators can decrypt passwords, directly contradicting SD-003 which mandates one-way bcrypt hashing (cost factor 12) and prohibits storing plaintext or recoverable passwords.
